copy.tl:
Anong mga gas ang bumubuo sa atmospera ng Mundo?

Ito ay humigit-kumulang 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, at 1% iba pang gas! Ang oxygen ang ginagamit natin para huminga.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga gas ang naghimo sa atmospera sa Yuta?

Kini mga 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, ug 1% ubang mga gas! Ang oxygen mao ang atong gigamit sa paghinga.

copy.en:
Where do all our weather events happen?

In the troposphere! It is the lowest layer of the atmosphere (0–12 km) where rain, clouds, and storms occur.
copy.tl:
Saan nangyayari ang lahat ng uri ng panahon?

Sa troposphere! Ito ang pinakamababang layer ng atmospera (0–12 km) kung saan nangyayari ang ulan, ulap, at bagyo.
copy.bis:
Asa mahitabo ang tanan nga matang sa panahon?

Sa troposphere! Mao ni ang pinakaubos nga layer sa atmospera (0–12 km) kung diin mahitabo ang ulan, panganod, ug bagyo.

copy.en: Air pressure decreases as altitude increases! At the top of a mountain, air is thinner and pressure is lower, making it hard to breathe.
copy.tl: Bumababa ang presyon ng hangin habang tumataas ang altitude! Sa ibabaw ng bundok, ang hangin ay mas manipis at mas mababa ang presyon, kaya nahihirapan huminga.
copy.bis: Manaog ang presyon sa hangin samtang mosaka ang altitude! Sa ibabaw sa bundok, ang hangin mas manipis ug mas ubos ang presyon, mao nga nahihirapan sa paghinga.

copy.en: Countries like the Maldives are made of atolls. Because they are so low, they are threatened by rising sea levels!
copy.tl: Ang mga bansa tulad ng Maldives ay binubuo ng mga atoll. Dahil napakababa nila, nanganganib sila sa pagtaas ng lebel ng dagat!
copy.bis: Ang mga nasod sama sa Maldives gilangkuban sa mga atoll. Tungod kay ubos kaayo sila, namiligro sila sa pagtaas sa lebel sa dagat!

copy.en: Believe it or not, an atom is mostly just empty space surrounding a tiny nucleus!
copy.tl: Sa totoo lang, ang atomo ay halos puro empty space na nakapalibot sa maliit na nucleus!
copy.bis: Sa tinuod lang, ang atomo halos puro empty space nga naglibot sa gamay nga nucleus!

copy.en: An atom is mostly empty space! It has a tiny nucleus at the center, surrounded by a huge space where the light electrons zoom around.
copy.tl: Halos walang laman ang loob ng atom! May napakaliit na nucleus sa gitna na napapaligiran ng malawak na puwang kung saan gumagalaw ang mga magagaan na electron.
copy.bis: Halos walay sulod ang atom! Adunay gamay kaayo nga nucleus sa tunga nga gilibutan og dako nga puwang diin naglihok ang gaan nga mga electron.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it has an equal number of protons and electrons! Their positive and negative charges cancel each other out perfectly.

copy.en:
Why is a normal atom neutral?

Because it has an equal number of protons and electrons! Their positive and negative charges cancel each other out perfectly.
copy.tl:
Bakit neutral ang isang normal na atomo?

Dahil pantay ang bilang ng proton at electron nito! Magkakansela ang positibo at negatibong charge nila.
copy.bis:
Nganong neutral ang normal nga atomo?

Tungod kay patas ang gidaghanon sa proton ug elektron! Magkansela ang positibo ug negatibong charge nila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the number of protons perfectly equals the number of electrons

copy.en: In a neutral atom, the number of protons perfectly equals the number of electrons!
copy.tl: Sa isang neutral na atomo, ang bilang ng proton ay eksaktong katumbas ng bilang ng electron!
copy.bis: Sa usa ka neutral nga atomo, ang gidaghanon sa proton eksakto nga managsama sa gidaghanon sa electron!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a property of neutral atoms (equal proton and electron counts) but does not differentiate protons, neutrons, and electrons by symbol, mass, charge, or location as required by the competency. It only touches on charge cancellation, not the comparative differentiation.

copy.en: In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons! Their positive and negative charges cancel out, leaving the atom with no overall charge.
copy.tl: Sa neutral na atom, magkapareho ang bilang ng proton at electron! Nagkakanselahan ang positive at negative charges nila, kaya walang kabuuang charge ang atom.
copy.bis: Sa neutral nga atom, managsama ang gidaghanon sa proton ug electron! Magkanselar ang ilang positive ug negative charges, busa walay kinatibuk-ang charge ang atom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is the dense, heavy center where protons and neutrons sit together! Almost all the atom's mass is found right here.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is the dense, heavy center where protons and neutrons sit together! Almost all the atom's mass is found right here.

copy.en: The nucleus is the dense, heavy center where protons and neutrons sit together! Almost all the atom's mass is found right here.
copy.tl: Ang nucleus ay ang siksik at mabigat na gitna kung saan magkasama ang protons at neutrons! Dito nakatago ang halos buong bigat ng atomo.
copy.bis: Ang nucleus mao ang siksik ug bug-at nga tunga diin nagkahiusa ang protons ug neutrons! Dinhi nahimutang ang halos tibuok gibug-aton sa atomo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The nucleus is super tiny compared to the whole atom, but it holds almost all the atom's mass because all the protons and neutrons are packed inside!

copy.en: The nucleus is super tiny compared to the whole atom, but it holds almost all the atom's mass because all the protons and neutrons are packed inside!
copy.tl: Napakaliit ng nucleus kumpara sa buong atom, pero dito nakatago ang halos lahat ng bigat ng atom dahil nandito ang mga proton at neutron!
copy.bis: Gamay ra kaayo ang nucleus kompara sa tibuok atom, apan dinhi natipon ang halos tanang gibug-aton kay naa diri ang mga proton ug neutron!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The three main parts of an atom are the proton, neutron, and electron!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the three subatomic particles. It does not draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells, which is the required action. Naming the particles is useful background but does not directly support the drawing skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The three main parts of an atom are the proton, neutron, and electron!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies the three particles but does not differentiate them by symbol, mass, charge, or location within an atom. This is foundational knowledge for the competency but does not directly teach the differentiation required.

copy.en: The three main parts of an atom are the proton, neutron, and electron! That makes three tiny pieces!
copy.tl: Ang tatlong pangunahing bahagi ng atomo ay ang proton, neutron, at electron! Tatlong maliliit na bahagi iyan!
copy.bis: Ang tulo ka nag-unang bahin sa atomo mao ang proton, neutron, ug electron! Tulo ka gamay nga bahin na!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every single atom is built from three main tiny particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card only names the three subatomic particles. It does not differentiate them by symbol, mass, charge, or location, which is the core action of G8-M-3. Naming them is useful background but does not directly teach the differentiation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every single atom is built from three main tiny particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the three particles but does not mention the nucleus or electron shells, nor does it ask for a drawing. It shares the broad topic of atomic structure but provides no direct instructional support for drawing the atom's structure.

copy.en: Every single atom is built from three main tiny particles: protons, neutrons, and electrons!
copy.tl: Ang bawat atomo ay binubuo ng tatlong pangunahing maliliit na particles: protons, neutrons, at electrons!
copy.bis: Ang matag atomo gilangkuban sa tulo ka nag-unang gagmay nga particles: protons, neutrons, ug electrons!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This number is roughly the total protons and neutrons inside the element's atom.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom

copy.en: Each box in the periodic table shows an atomic mass! This number is roughly the total protons and neutrons inside the element's atom.
copy.tl: Bawat kahon sa periodic table ay may atomic mass! Ito ay halos katumbas ng kabuuang bilang ng proton at neutron sa atomo ng elemento.
copy.bis: Ang matag kahon sa periodic table adunay atomic mass! Kini halos katumbas sa kinatibuk-ang gidaghanon sa proton ug neutron sa atomo sa elemento.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even smaller particles called quarks make up protons and neutrons.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that quarks are smaller than atoms and make up protons and neutrons. It does not differentiate protons, neutrons, and electrons by symbol, mass, charge, or location, which is the core action of G8-M-3. The content is topically related to subatomic particles but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Think atoms are the smallest things ever? Nope! Even smaller particles called quarks make up protons and neutrons. Atoms are small, but not the smallest!
copy.tl: Akala mo ang atomo ang pinakamaliit na bagay? Hindi! May mas maliliit pa na quark na bumubuo sa proton at neutron. Maliit ang atomo, pero hindi pinakamaliit!
copy.bis: Naghunahuna ka nga ang atomo ang pinakagamay nga butang? Dili! Naa pa'y mas gagmay nga quark nga naghimo sa proton ug neutron. Gamay ang atomo, apan dili pinakagamay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The chips inside cellphones and laptops have parts only a few atoms wide!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses atoms in computer chips and how engineers' understanding of atoms enables technology, but it does not ask students to identify a specific science invention from home or the local community or explain its impact on everyday life. The content is only tangentially related to the competency's focus on identifying inventions and their impacts.

copy.en:
How do atoms make our phones and laptops work?

The chips inside cellphones and laptops have parts only a few atoms wide! Our everyday tech works because engineers understand atoms.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang mga cellphone at laptop dahil sa atomo?

Ang mga chip sa cellphone at laptop ay may bahaging ilang atomo lang ang laki! Gumagana ang teknolohiyang ginagamit natin araw-araw dahil nauunawaan ng mga engineer ang atomo.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglihok sa cellphone ug laptop tungod sa atomo?

Ang mga chip sa cellphone ug laptop adunay mga bahin nga pipila ra ka atomo ang gilapdon! Molihok ang teknolohiya nga atong gamiton kada adlaw tungod kay nasabtan sa mga engineer ang atomo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: atoms themselves aren't alive! They don't eat, breathe, or grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card contrasts atoms with living things and mentions that living things do not eat, breathe, or grow, but it does not teach the observable difference between living and non-living things using local examples. assignedReviews.card_evidence: They don't eat, breathe, or grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

copy.en: Living things like plants and people are made of atoms, but atoms themselves aren't alive! They don't eat, breathe, or grow — yet together they build living things.
copy.tl: Ang mga buhay tulad ng halaman at tao ay gawa sa atomo, pero ang atomo mismo ay hindi buhay! Hindi ito kumakain, humihinga, o lumalaki — pero magkakasama, nabubuo ang buhay.
copy.bis: Ang buhi nga mga butang sama sa tanom ug tawo hinimo sa atomo, apan ang atomo mismo dili buhi! Dili kini mokaon, moginhawa, o motubo — apan magkahiusa sila, mahimo ang buhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different gases make different colors! Green and red come from oxygen, while purple and blue come from nitrogen high in the air.

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains which gases produce which aurora colors but does not explain how energy from the Sun interacts with the atmosphere. No mention of solar energy, particles, or the interaction mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different gases make different colors! Green and red come from oxygen, while purple and blue come from nitrogen high in the air.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card names oxygen and nitrogen as gases in the air, but it does not describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. It only mentions two gases in the context of aurora colors, not the composition of air as a mixture.

copy.en:
Why do auroras glow in different colors?

Different gases make different colors! Green and red come from oxygen, while purple and blue come from nitrogen high in the air.
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-iiba-iba ang kulay ng aurora?

Iba't ibang gases ang gumagawa ng iba't ibang kulay! Ang berde at pula ay galing sa oxygen, ang lila at asul ay galing sa nitrogen sa mataas na hangin.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lahi-lahi ang kolor sa aurora?

Lain-laing gases ang mohimo og lain-laing kolor! Ang berde ug pula gikan sa oxygen, samtang ang purple ug asul gikan sa nitrogen sa taas nga hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An aurora is usually silent! It happens so high up where the air is too thin to carry sound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that sound cannot travel in very thin air at high altitudes, which touches on sound transfer but is not an everyday situation like a ringing bell or hearing noises. It does not directly support the competency's focus on exploring and describing sound in everyday contexts.

copy.en: An aurora is usually silent! It happens so high up where the air is too thin to carry sound, though a few people hear faint noises.
copy.tl: Karaniwang tahimik ang aurora! Nangyayari ito nang napakataas kung saan napakanipis ng hangin para magdala ng tunog, kahit may ilang tao ang nakakarinig ng banayad na tunog.
copy.bis: Kasagaran hilom ang aurora! Mahitabo kini sa hilabihan ka taas diin nipis kaayo ang hangin aron magdala og tingog, bisan adunay pipila ka tawo nga makadungog og hinay nga tingog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: more auxin gathers on the shaded side of a stem, making cells there grow longer so the stem bends toward the light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific plant response mechanism (phototropism via auxin), which is an example of a living thing responding and growing. However, the Grade 3 competency asks students to describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The card does not teach these characteristics as a general concept; it only provides a specialized example far beyond the grade level, so it does not directly support the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en:
Why do stems bend toward light?

In phototropism, more auxin gathers on the shaded side of a stem, making cells there grow longer so the stem bends toward the light.
copy.tl:
Bakit yumuyuko ang tangkay papunta sa liwanag?

Sa phototropism, mas maraming auxin ang napupunta sa bahaging may anino, kaya mas humahaba ang mga cell doon at yumuyuko ang tangkay papunta sa liwanag.
copy.bis:
Nganong moyuko ang punoan paingon sa kahayag?

Sa phototropism, mas daghang auxin ang moadto sa kilid nga may landong, mao nga mas motaas ang mga selula didto ug moyuko ang punoan paingon sa kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If you move at a constant speed the whole time, average speed equals it exactly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses average speed versus constant speed but does not define speed as distance over time, which is the core of G4-F-3. It assumes prior knowledge of speed and does not directly support identifying the definition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If you move at a constant speed the whole time, average speed equals it exactly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions constant speed but does not involve constructing or labeling graphs, nor does it address stationary or uniform speeds in a graphical context. It only conceptually contrasts average and constant speed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: But if you speed up and slow down, average speed falls between your fastest and slowest.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and annotate distance-time graphs and velocity-time graphs to represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on speeding up and slowing down, which relates to non-uniform motion, but it does not construct or annotate distance-time or velocity-time graphs, nor does it represent uniform and non-uniform acceleration as required by G8-F-3.

copy.en:
Is average speed always the same as your actual speed?

Not always! If you move at a constant speed the whole time, average speed equals it exactly. But if you speed up and slow down, average speed falls between your fastest and slowest.
copy.tl:
Laging pareho ba ang average speed sa totoong bilis mo?

Hindi laging pareho! Kung constant ang takbo mo, ang average speed ay katumbas niyon. Kung bumibilis at bumabagal ka, ang average speed ay nasa pagitan ng pinakamabilis at pinakamabagal.
copy.bis:
Parehas ba kanunay ang average speed sa imong tinuod nga tulin?

Dili kanunay parehas! Kung constant ang dagan, ang average speed parehas sa constant speed. Kung mopaspas ug mohinay, ang average speed anaa sa tunga sa pinakapaspas ug pinakahinay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Multiply speed by time for distance, or divide distance by speed for time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the speed formula to rearrange for distance/time but does not identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed. It assumes the definition rather than teaching it.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Multiply speed by time for distance, or divide distance by speed for time.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about calculating distance/time from speed, not about measuring distance and time using simple equipment. No measurement or equipment is involved.

copy.en:
How can you find distance or time if you already know your average speed?

Just rearrange the formula! Multiply speed by time for distance, or divide distance by speed for time. For example, 5 m/s for 10 seconds is 50 meters!
copy.tl:
Paano mo malalaman ang layo o oras kung alam mo na ang average speed mo?

I-rearrange lang ang formula! I-multiply ang speed sa time para makuha ang distance, o hatiin ang distance sa speed. Halimbawa, 5 m/s sa 10 segundo ay 50 metro!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagkahibalo sa gilay-on o oras kung nahibaloan na nimo ang imong average speed?

I-rearrange lang ang formula! I-multiply ang speed sa time para makuha ang distance, o bahina ang distance sa speed. Pananglitan, 5 m/s sa 10 segundo kay 50 metros!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a player's time drops over the same distance, their average speed is higher
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the concept of average speed and its relationship to time and distance, but it does not explicitly identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed. It focuses on using average speed as a progress indicator, not on defining speed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a player's time drops over the same distance, their average speed is higher
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions time and distance but does not involve measuring distance and time using simple equipment. It is about interpreting average speed, not about the measurement process itself.

copy.en:
How do coaches know if an athlete is getting better?

They use average speed! If a player's time drops over the same distance, their average speed is higher, which is a clear sign of progress.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga coach kung gumagaling ang atleta?

Ginagamit nila ang average speed! Kung mas mababa ang oras ng manlalaro sa parehong distansya, mas mataas ang average speed niya, na palatandaan ng pag-unlad.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsusi sa mga coach kung nag-uswag ang atleta?

Mabati sa receptors sa imong blood vessels ang pagbag-o ug magsignal sa utok, nga maoy mosulti sa kasingkasing nga mopaspas ang pitik aron maibalik ang pressure.

Ito ay bihirang lumulutang na bola ng liwanag tuwing may bagyo! Napakabihira nito kaya hindi pa lubos na nauunawaan ng mga siyentipiko kung paano ito nabubuo.

Usa kini ka talagsaon nga naglutaw nga bola sa kahayag panahon sa bagyo! Talagsaon kaayo mao nga wala pa hingpit nga masabti sa mga siyentipiko kung giunsa kini pagporma.

Mapuno ni sa imong giginhawa! Sagol ni sa nitrogen, oxygen, ug mas daghang carbon dioxide, kay nagamit na sa imong lawas ang ubang oxygen.

assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a practical example of using a banana leaf as insulation to keep food warm, but it does not identify or explain conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it name any heat-transfer mechanism. It only illustrates a general effect of reducing heat loss, which is related background but not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: Wrap your rice or bibingka in a banana leaf! It acts like a cozy blanket to keep your food warm longer.
copy.tl: Balutin ang kanin o bibingka sa dahon ng saging! Parang kumot ito para manatiling mainit ang pagkain nang mas matagal.
copy.bis: Iputos ang kanin o bibingka sa dahon sa saging! Sama kini og kumot aron magpabilin nga init ang pagkaon og mas dugay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wide banana leaves are used as a natural wrapper
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but only as a food wrapper; it does not address the role of leaves in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wide banana leaves are used as a natural wrapper
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a human use of a plant part, not how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. No interdependence is taught.

copy.en: Wide banana leaves are used as a natural wrapper for foods like suman and other rice cakes.
copy.tl: Ang malalapad na dahon ng saging ay ginagamit bilang likas na pambalot ng pagkain tulad ng suman at iba pang kakanin.
copy.bis: Ang lapad nga dahon sa saging gigamit isip natural nga putos sa pagkaon sama sa suman ug uban pang kakanin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It slows the escape of heat so your food stays hot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that wrapping rice in banana leaves keeps it warm by slowing heat escape, but it does not identify or distinguish conduction, convection, or radiation. It only addresses heat retention generally, without naming any of the three heat-transfer modes required by the competency.

copy.en:
Why wrap rice in banana leaves?

Wrapping rice in a banana leaf or cloth keeps it warm! It slows the escape of heat so your food stays hot.
copy.tl:
Bakit binabalot ang kanin sa dahon ng saging?

Ang pagbalot ng kanin sa dahon ng saging o tela ay nagpapanatiling mainit! Pinipigilan nito ang pagtakas ng init.
copy.bis:
Nganong giputos ang kan-on sa dahon sa saging?

Ang pagputos sa kan-on sa dahon sa saging o panapton magpabiling init niini! Gipugngan niini ang pag-ikyas sa kainit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: slow down soil erosion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions soil erosion but only as something the terraces slow down; it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials, which is the core action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Banaue rice terraces were carved into mountainsides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a human-made terrace, not a natural landform such as a mountain, valley, river, or coastline, and it does not describe how the feature influences living or non-living components of the environment.

copy.en: The Banaue rice terraces were carved into mountainsides to make flat land for growing rice and to slow down soil erosion!
copy.tl: Ang hagdan-hagdang palayan ng Banaue ay inukit sa mountainsides para gawing patag ang lupa para sa palay at pigilan ang soil erosion!
copy.bis: Ang hagdan-hagdan nga humayan sa Banaue gikulit sa mountainsides aron mahimong patag ang yuta para sa humay ug mapugngan ang soil erosion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The wide, flat end of a paddle pushes more water with each stroke!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how the shape of a paddle affects the strength of a push, but it does not demonstrate or describe using pushes/pulls to change speed or direction (faster, slower, turn, stop). It is about force magnitude due to shape, not about changing motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The wide, flat end of a paddle pushes more water with each stroke!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pushing water with a paddle, which is a way people make objects move, but it does not explore or demonstrate different ways to make objects move; it only describes how blade shape affects the strength of a push. It is background knowledge about force, not a direct exploration of moving objects.

copy.en: The wide, flat end of a paddle pushes more water with each stroke! If the tip were narrow, it would grab less water and give a much weaker forward push.
copy.tl: Ang lapad at patag na dulo ng sagwan ay nakakatulak ng mas maraming tubig sa bawat hila! Kung makitid ito, kaunti lang ang maaabot kaya mas mahina ang pasulong.
copy.bis: Ang lapad ug patag nga tumoy sa bugsay makadoso ug mas daghang tubig sa matag bira! Kung nipis ra kini, gamay ra ang maabot nga tubig maong mas huyang ang pagpaunahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: water clings and pulls back along its sides, called drag or water resistance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water resistance (drag) as a force opposing motion, which is conceptually related to friction, but it does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it address the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces. It only mentions a single surface (water) and no experimental procedure.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you must keep paddling to maintain your speed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate in practical situations and describe that acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction as the result of a net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies that paddling counteracts water resistance to maintain speed, which touches on net force and constant velocity, but it does not demonstrate or describe acceleration as a change in speed and/or direction. No acceleration is discussed; the focus is on maintaining constant speed against drag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you must keep paddling to maintain your speed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a situation where paddling balances water resistance to maintain speed, which is an example of balanced forces (constant velocity). However, it does not explicitly identify or describe balanced vs. unbalanced forces, nor does it contrast with an unbalanced force example. The competency requires identifying and describing everyday situations demonstrating both balanced and unbalanced forces; the card only hints at one balanced-force scenario without the required description.

copy.en:
Why must you keep paddling a banca?

As the banca moves, water clings and pulls back along its sides, called drag or water resistance! That is why you must keep paddling to maintain your speed.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan mong magsagwan ulit?

Habang gumagalaw ang banca, kumakapit at humihila pabalik ang tubig sa gilid nito—ito ang tinatawag na drag o hadlang ng tubig! Kaya kailangan mong magsagwan ulit para mapanatili ang bilis.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga kinahanglan ka magbugsay balik?

Samtang molihok ang banca, ang tubig mokapyot ug mobira pabalik sa kilid niini—kini gitawag nga drag o sukol sa tubig! Mao nga kinahanglan ka magbugsay balik aron mapadayon ang katulin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reducing resistance so they tire less
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes reducing drag (fluid friction) by tilting the paddle, but does not demonstrate friction producing heat nor investigate ways of increasing friction. It only touches on reducing resistance, which is a peripheral aspect of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tilt the paddle blade flat when swinging it forward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions changing the blade's orientation to reduce resistance, but does not explore or describe how size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture affect movement. The blade's shape is implied but not described as a factor affecting movement in the sense of the competency.

copy.en: Skilled paddlers tilt the paddle blade flat when swinging it forward! This stops it from slapping the wind or splashing water, reducing resistance so they tire less.
copy.tl: Ikiniling ng mga sanay na tagasagwan nang patag ang dulo kapag ibinabalik ito! Para hindi humampas sa hangin o sumalpok sa tubig, nababawasan ang hadlang kaya hindi sila gaanong napapagod.
copy.bis: Ikiling sa hanas nga magbubugsay nga patag ang tumoy kung ibalik kini! Aron dili mosagpa sa hangin o motalsik sa tubig, makaminus sa sukol maong dili kaayo kapuyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Barangay radios and halls repeat the PHIVOLCS alert!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains how PHIVOLCS alerts are broadcast through barangay radios and halls. It does not teach interpreting alert levels or demonstrate specific actions before, during, and after a volcanic eruption, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How do people without internet know the PHIVOLCS alert?

Barangay radios and halls repeat the PHIVOLCS alert! This helps everyone hear if they should stay, pack, or leave.
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman ng walang internet ang alerto ng PHIVOLCS?

Inuulit ng mga radyo at bulwagan ng barangay ang alerto ng PHIVOLCS! Naririnig ng walang internet kung mananatili, mag-eempake, o aalis.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo sa walay internet sa alerto sa PHIVOLCS?

Gibalik-balik sa mga radyo ug hall sa barangay ang alerto sa PHIVOLCS! Makadungog ang walay internet kung magpabilin, mag-empake, o molakaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A tree's outer bark is dead and can't stretch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer plant part (bark) but does not address the role of leaves, roots, or stems in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only shares a fact about bark cracking due to growth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the tree keeps growing wider underneath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses tree growth and bark cracking, not the root and shoot system or why they are important. No direct support for observing or describing root/shoot systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the tree keeps growing wider underneath
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates growth (the tree grows wider) but does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) as a set. It only gives a specific example of bark cracking, not a description of growth as a characteristic.

copy.en: A tree's outer bark is dead and can't stretch, but the tree keeps growing wider underneath — so the bark cracks into deep grooves as it's pushed apart.
copy.tl: Patay na ang panlabas na balat ng puno kaya hindi na ito lumalaki, pero patuloy na lumalapad ang puno sa loob — kaya nabibiyak ito at nagkakaroon ng malalalim na guhit.
copy.bis: Patay na ang gawas nga panit sa kahoy mao nga dili na motubo, apan padayon nga molapad ang kahoy sa sulod — mao nga mabuak kini ug maghimog lawom nga mga gilis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a small careful cut is made through the tree's bark so the sap drips out
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bark, an outer part of a plant, but does not describe the role of leaves, roots, or stems in obtaining water and nutrients from soil. It only describes sap collection, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To collect sap like rubber, a small careful cut is made through the tree's bark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns useful things made from non-living materials and the natural materials used. Sap is a product of a living tree, not a non-living material, and the card does not identify a manufactured item or its natural non-living source.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To collect sap like rubber, a small careful cut is made through the tree's bark
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a process of collecting sap but does not identify a specific science invention from home or community or explain its impact on everyday life. Rubber production is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: To collect sap like rubber, a small careful cut is made through the tree's bark so the sap drips out — done gently so the tree doesn't die.
copy.tl: Para makakuha ng dagta gaya ng goma, ginagawan ng maliit na hiwa ang balat ng puno para tumulo ang dagta — ginagawa itong maingat para hindi mamatay ang puno.
copy.bis: Aron makakuha og dagta sama sa goma, gibutangan og gamay nga samad ang panit sa kahoy aron motulo ang dagta — buhaton kini og maampingon aron dili mamatay ang kahoy.
